questions.question: Eight years ago, the ratio of the ages of P and Q was 2:3. Eight years hence, the ratio of their ages will be 3:4. What is Q's present age?
questions.solution:
Q.2 Solution:• Correct Answer: C• Section: General Aptitude | Sub-topic: Quantitative Aptitude | Type: MCQ | Marks: 1Q.2   |  Topic: Quantitative Aptitude  |  [MCQ · 1 mark]Question:Eight years ago, the ratio of the ages of P and Q was 2:3. Eight years hence, the ratio of their ages will be 3:4. What is Q's present age?(A) 40 years(B) 48 years(C) 56 years(D) 64 yearsAnswer: (C)Explanation:Let the ages 8 years ago be 2x and 3x for P and Q. Present ages: P=2x+8, Q=3x+8. Eight years hence: P=2x+16, Q=3x+16. Given (2x+16)/(3x+16)=3/4, cross-multiplying: 4(2x+16)=3(3x+16) => 8x+64=9x+48 => x=16. Q's present age = 3(16)+8 = 56 years. Check: 8 years ago, P=32, Q=48 (ratio 2:3, correct); 8 years hence, P=48, Q=64 (ratio 3:4, correct).Why the other options are incorrect:(A) 40 results from solving for x incorrectly and applying it to the wrong person's age formula.(B) 48 is Q's age 8 years ago (3x with x=16), mistakenly reported as the present age.(D) 64 is Q's age 8 years hence, mistakenly reported instead of the present age.

questions.question: Question 6

options.A: cistern can be filled by pipe X in 15 hours and by pipe Y in 10 hours. Pipe Z, when opened alone on a full cistern, can empty it in 12 hours. All three pipes are opened together when the cistern is empty, and pipe Z is closed after 3 hours (X and Y continue running). How many additional hours from the moment Z is closed will it take to fill the cistern completely?

questions.solution:
Q.6 Solution:• Correct Answer: C• Section: General Aptitude | Sub-topic: Quantitative Aptitude | Type: MCQ | Marks: 2Q.6   |  Topic: Quantitative Aptitude  |  [MCQ · 2 marks]Question:A cistern can be filled by pipe X in 15 hours and by pipe Y in 10 hours. Pipe Z, when opened alone on a full cistern, can empty it in 12 hours. All three pipes are opened together when the cistern is empty, and pipe Z is closed after 3 hours (X and Y continue running). How many additional hours from the moment Z is closed will it take to fill the cistern completely?(A) 3.6 hours(B) 4.0 hours(C) 4.5 hours(D) 5.4 hoursAnswer: (C)Explanation:Rates (cistern/hour): X=1/15, Y=1/10, Z=-1/12. Combined rate for first 3 hours = 1/15+1/10-1/12 = 4/60+6/60-5/60 = 5/60 = 1/12 per hour. Fraction filled in 3 hours = 3/12 = 1/4. Remaining fraction = 3/4. After Z is closed, combined rate of X and Y = 1/15+1/10 = 2/30+3/30 = 5/30 = 1/6 per hour. Time to fill remaining 3/4 = (3/4)/(1/6) = 4.5 hours.Why the other options are incorrect:(A) 3.6 hours would result from a computational slip in the fraction already filled during the first 3 hours.(B) 4.0 hours results from a minor arithmetic rounding error in combining the rates of X and Y.(D) 5.4 hours results from using the original three-pipe combined rate (1/12) instead of switching to only X and Y's rate for the second phase.

questions.question: The average of 9 consecutive even numbers is 42. If the largest number is increased by 25% and the smallest number is decreased by 10% (all other numbers remaining unchanged), what is the new average of all 9 numbers? (Round to one decimal place.)
questions.solution:
Q.7 Solution:• Correct Answer: B• Section: General Aptitude | Sub-topic: Quantitative Aptitude | Type: MCQ | Marks: 2Q.7   |  Topic: Quantitative Aptitude  |  [MCQ · 2 marks]Question:The average of 9 consecutive even numbers is 42. If the largest number is increased by 25% and the smallest number is decreased by 10% (all other numbers remaining unchanged), what is the new average of all 9 numbers? (Round to one decimal place.)(A) 42.3(B) 43.0(C) 43.8(D) 44.5Answer: (B)Explanation:For 9 consecutive even numbers with average 42, the middle (5th) number is 42, so the numbers range symmetrically: 34,36,38,40,42,44,46,48,50 (sum = 9x42 = 378). Largest = 50; increased by 25% gives 50x1.25 = 62.5, an increase of 12.5. Smallest = 34; decreased by 10% gives 34x0.9 = 30.6, a decrease of 3.4. New sum = 378+12.5-3.4 = 387.1. New average = 387.1/9 = 43.011, which rounds to 43.0.Why the other options are incorrect:(A) 42.3 results from applying the percentage changes to the average (42) rather than to the actual largest and smallest numbers.(C) 43.8 results from increasing the smallest number instead of decreasing it, effectively adding rather than subtracting its change.(D) 44.5 results from applying both percentage changes as increases, ignoring that the smallest number is meant to decrease.

questions.question: Five silos A, B, C, D, E are arranged in a straight row, numbered from position 1 (leftmost) to position 5 (rightmost), not necessarily in that order. The following is known:(i) B is immediately to the right of E.(ii) D is at one of the two ends of the row.(iii) There are exactly two silos between A and C.(iv) B is not at either end of the row.(v) A is to the left of C.(vi) C is immediately adjacent to D.Which silo occupies the middle (3rd) position?
questions.solution:
Q.9 Solution:• Correct Answer: B• Section: General Aptitude | Sub-topic: Analytical Aptitude | Type: MCQ | Marks: 2Q.9   |  Topic: Analytical Aptitude  |  [MCQ · 2 marks]Question:Five silos A, B, C, D, E are arranged in a straight row, numbered from position 1 (leftmost) to position 5 (rightmost), not necessarily in that order. The following is known:(i) B is immediately to the right of E.(ii) D is at one of the two ends of the row.(iii) There are exactly two silos between A and C.(iv) B is not at either end of the row.(v) A is to the left of C.(vi) C is immediately adjacent to D.Which silo occupies the middle (3rd) position?(A) A(B) B(C) C(D) DAnswer: (B)Explanation:Let position(E) = position(B) - 1, from clue (i); position(B) is 2, 3, or 4 from clue (iv). Testing position(B)=3, E=2: clue (ii) requires D at 1 or 5. If D=1, remaining positions {4,5} for A,C give a gap of only 1, violating clue (iii) (needs a gap of 3). If D=5, remaining positions {1,4} for A,C give |A-C|=3, satisfying clue (iii); with clue (v) A is left of C, so A=1, C=4. Clue (vi) requires C adjacent to D: C=4, D=5 -- adjacent, satisfied. This gives the unique arrangement: A(1)-E(2)-B(3)-C(4)-D(5). (Testing B=4 similarly yields a candidate arrangement, but clue (vi) eliminates it since C and D are not adjacent in that case.) Hence the silo in the middle (3rd) position is B.Why the other options are incorrect:(A) A occupies position 1, not the middle position.(C) C occupies position 4, not the middle position.(D) D occupies position 5 (an end), not the middle position.

questions.question: In the Newton-Raphson method for finding a root of f(x)=0, the iteration formula is x(n+1) = x(n) - f(x(n))/f'(x(n)). For f(x) = x^2 - 5 and a starting guess x0 = 2, what is x1?
questions.solution:

For f(x) = x^2 - 5 and a starting guess x0 = 2, what is x1?(A) 2.20(B) 2.25(C) 2.30(D) 2.50Answer: (B)Explanation:f(2) = 2^2-5 = -1. f'(x) = 2x, so f'(2) = 4. x1 = x0 - f(x0)/f'(x0) = 2 - (-1)/4 = 2 + 0.25 = 2.25.Why the other options are incorrect:(A) 2.20 results from a slightly incorrect value of the correction term, e.g. using f'(2)=5 instead of the correct 4.(C) 2.30 results from a small arithmetic slip in computing f(2)/f'(2).(D) 2.50 results from omitting the derivative entirely and simply adding f(x0)'s magnitude (1/2) using a wrong denominator.

options.A: The hydrograph of direct runoff resulting from one unit depth (e.g. 1 cm) of effective rainfall occurring uniformly over the watershed in a unit time
options.B: The hydrograph representing base flow only, excluding direct surface runoff
options.C: A hydrograph normalized to have unit peak discharge, regardless of the rainfall depth that produced it
options.D: The hydrograph of a single, unit-sized sub-watershed within a larger drainage basin

questions.solution:

questions.question: Which of the following best defines the "equilibrium moisture content" (EMC) of a grain?

options.A: The moisture content at which the grain neither gains nor loses moisture when exposed to air of a given temperature and relative humidity
options.B: The moisture content of the grain at harvest time
options.C: The moisture content at which the drying rate is at its maximum
options.D: The moisture content below which the grain becomes brittle and prone to cracking

questions.question: For a solid or fluid-containing body undergoing transient heat transfer (e.g. a cylindrical milk storage tank losing heat by conduction through its wall and then convection to ambient air), which non-dimensional number represents the ratio of internal conductive resistance to external convective resistance, and is used to judge whether a simple lumped-capacitance analysis is valid?

A small Biot number (typically Bi < 0.1) indicates that internal conduction resistance is negligible compared to external convection, justifying the lumped-capacitance (uniform-temperature) approximation.Why the other options are incorrect:(A) The Reynolds number characterizes the ratio of inertial to viscous forces in fluid flow, relevant to determining laminar/turbulent flow regimes, not internal-versus-external heat transfer resistance.(C) The Prandtl number relates momentum diffusivity to thermal diffusivity of a fluid, used in convective heat transfer correlations, not for assessing lumped-capacitance validity.(D) The Nusselt number is the ratio of convective to conductive heat transfer across a fluid boundary layer, used to determine the convective heat transfer coefficient itself, not to compare internal versus external resistances of a solid body.

questions.question: The function f(x,y) = x^2 + y^2 - 4x - 6y + 13 has a stationary point. Determine the nature of this stationary point.
questions.solution:
Q.36 Solution:• Correct Answer: A• Section: Engineering Mathematics | Sub-topic: Calculus | Type: MCQ | Marks: 2Q.36   |  Topic: Calculus  |  [MCQ · 2 marks]Question:The function f(x,y) = x^2 + y^2 - 4x - 6y + 13 has a stationary point. Determine the nature of this stationary point.(A) Local minimum(B) Local maximum(C) Saddle point(D) Point of inflectionAnswer: (A)Explanation:First-order conditions: fx = 2x-4 = 0 gives x=2; fy = 2y-6 = 0 gives y=3, so the stationary point is (2,3). Second derivatives: fxx=2, fyy=2, fxy=0. Discriminant D = fxx.fyy - (fxy)^2 = 2x2 - 0 = 4 > 0, and fxx = 2 > 0. Since D>0 and fxx>0, the point (2,3) is a local minimum. (In fact, f(x,y) can be rewritten by completing the square as (x-2)^2+(y-3)^2+0, confirming a global minimum of value 0.)Why the other options are incorrect:(B) A local maximum would require D>0 with fxx<0, but fxx=2>0 here, ruling this out.(C) A saddle point would require D<0, but D=4>0 here, ruling this out.(D) "Point of inflection" is a concept for single-variable functions (a change in concavity); it is not the correct classification for a two-variable stationary point analysis, and in any case the second-derivative test here is conclusive.

(Select all that apply.)(A) A higher fluid velocity generally increases the convective heat transfer coefficient(B) The convective heat transfer coefficient depends on the fluid's thermophysical properties (density, viscosity, thermal conductivity, specific heat)(C) Natural (free) convection generally gives lower heat transfer coefficients than forced convection, for similar fluids(D) The convective heat transfer coefficient is a fixed material property of the fluid, independent of flow conditionsAnswer: (A, B, C)Explanation:Higher fluid velocity (A) increases turbulence and reduces boundary layer thickness, generally increasing the convective heat transfer coefficient h. The coefficient h depends on several thermophysical properties of the fluid (B), as reflected in dimensionless correlations (Nu, Re, Pr). Natural (free) convection, driven only by buoyancy, typically produces lower h values than forced convection at comparable conditions (C). Statement (D) is incorrect: unlike thermal conductivity (a true material property), the convective heat transfer coefficient h is NOT a fixed material property -- it depends strongly on flow velocity, geometry, and flow regime (laminar/turbulent), in addition to fluid properties.

(Select all that apply.)(A) Cream separation relies on the density difference between fat globules and skim milk(B) Higher centrifugal speed (higher g-force) generally increases separation efficiency, up to practical and mechanical limits(C) Fat globules, being less dense than skim milk, move toward the outer wall of the centrifuge bowl(D) Higher milk viscosity (such as in colder milk) generally improves separation efficiencyAnswer: (A, B)Explanation:Cream (fat) separation from skim milk fundamentally relies on the density difference between fat globules and the aqueous skim milk phase (A); increasing centrifugal g-force generally improves separation efficiency, up to the practical and mechanical limits of the equipment (B). Statement (C) is incorrect: because fat globules are LESS dense than skim milk, under centrifugal force they migrate toward the AXIS (centre) of rotation, not the outer wall -- the denser skim milk is what moves toward the outer wall. Statement (D) is also incorrect: higher viscosity (as in colder milk) INCREASES the resistance to fat globule movement and HINDERS separation; warming milk (reducing its viscosity) typically improves separation efficiency, which is why cream separators are usually operated on warmed milk.
